content: If you get a failure in Check {Mathlib, Tactic, Counterexamples, Archive}.lean actually caused by an error in validate lake-manifest.json inputRevs, please merge master

We sometimes make changes / fixes to CI which require essentially all open PRs to merge master to build properly (#mathlib4 > CI "lint style" failure @ 💬 was another recent case). I wonder if it'd be helpful to have an informational label like please-merge-master and some automation to apply it to all open (non-draft) PRs, possibly with some other conditions. Maybe it could be triggered by some keywords in the merged PR?

Sorry about this, I didn't anticipate it requiring everyone to merge master...

Even better than telling everyone they need to merge master would be doing it for them, perhaps.

In my organization's repos, we get a button on our PRs when the branch is out of sync with master -- we can merge master using one click on the github PR page. Would it be possible to configure mathlib repo to turn on this setting? It would allow contributors to merge master without having to start up a git client.
Yeah, it should be. I think we turned it off because it was too enticing for people even if there was no need to merge?
Is there a downside to merging master?
I'd be happy to enable the button if someone tells me where to find it!

Kim Morrison said:

Even better than telling everyone they need to merge master would be doing it for them, perhaps.

I'd rather leave control over merging in the hands of contributors -- it's possible that they have some local commits / changes that would be annoying to fix if we automatically merged. Though I guess maybe we could build in a way for people to opt out?
https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-suggestions-to-update-pull-request-branches

Ruben Van de Velde said:

Yeah, it should be. I think we turned it off because it was too enticing for people even if there was no need to merge?

Perhaps we can revisit that now that we switched to fork based PRs?
Thanks, enabled!
I'm fine with trying and seeing if we encounter any downsides

There also seems to be some warning (not error) about the cache:

**verify that everything was available in the cache**

Cache verification incomplete, but this PR's Cache/ differs from master's. CI wrote the cache with master's binary and this job reads it with the PR branch's, so a changed key space (such as a rootHashGeneration bump) misses as expected. Continuing; the cache repopulates once this lands on master.

The build seems to have completed normally otherwise, afaict.

I think this means you should merge master but I'm not sure. In any case should probably adjust the wording of the warning to be more actionable / possibly upgrade it to an error.
